field_semantics.change_specific: True iff the workflow has a path-filtered push-to-main trigger: its firing is attributable to the changed files, so its production consequences are the change's jurisdiction.
field_semantics.production_consequential: Property of the WORKFLOW, independent of trigger shape: True iff the workflow, when triggered, executes production-consequential actions (OIDC-minted live-runtime invocation, production ref writes, production promotion).
field_semantics.reviewed_at: Date a human last reviewed this file's classification against its exact bytes (sha256). Reset to null by --emit-manifest whenever the bytes change.
field_semantics.standing_ratification: Required when a workflow is production_consequential AND fires on unfiltered push-to-main (standing pipeline): the recorded authority for its standing production execution. status=RATIFIED (ratification document in-tree) or PLACEMENT_ONLY (director-placed bytes, no separate ratification document found — explicit, reviewable). workflow_run-only production workflows inherit authorization from their change-specific chain root.

rule: change-specific = path-filtered push-to-main triggers + workflow_run descendants; every-push workflows are the standing pipeline and cannot smuggle jurisdiction. Two enforcement layers: (1) the verdict gates each change's change-specific production chain; (2) the manifest curates EVERY push-to-main workflow, so the class cannot silently grow — an unfiltered production workflow without a standing_ratification record fails the freshness test. pull_request_target triggers are a different trigger class (PR-time, base-repo context with secrets) and are out of scope for this push-to-main gate.
